name: Azure Monitor
description: Azure Monitor and Microsoft Entra diagnostic exports as the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services lands them: who signed in or made a change, from where, to what, and how it came out, across Entra ID, Intune, Azure Activity Log and Cosmos DB data-plane logs, plus VM performance-counter aggregates.
source: Microsoft Entra activity log schema pages, the Microsoft Graph auditEvent (Intune) and Azure Activity Log event schema references, the Azure Cosmos DB diagnostic-log sample and the WADMetrics storage schema, read against live field captures from a Splunk instance seeded with Splunk_TA_microsoft_cloud_services data.

earliest.label: since
earliest.hint: On _time, which the add-on sets from the record's own time field.

latest.label: until
latest.hint: Optional. Event Hub delivery can lag the source event by minutes.

index.label: index
index.placeholder: the index the record landed in
index.hint: Taken from the event you clicked when known.

feed.label: Azure Monitor
feed.description: Azure Monitor and Microsoft Entra diagnostic exports as the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services lands them: Entra sign-in and audit activity, Intune device-management audit events, Azure Activity Log administrative events, Cosmos DB data-plane requests and VM performance-counter aggregates.

tenant_id.label: Tenant id
tenant_id.description: The Microsoft Entra tenant a record belongs to, a GUID. Seen as tenantId, properties.tenantId and body.tenantId across the family.

correlation_id.label: Correlation id
correlation_id.description: Ties together the records one request or operation produced.

category.label: Log category
category.description: Which kind of record this is: the family's discriminator (SignInLogs, AuditLogs, DataPlaneRequests and the rest).

operation_name.label: Operation name
operation_name.description: The friendly name of the action the record describes, for example Add member to role or ReadFeed.

actor_principal.label: Actor principal name
actor_principal.description: The human-readable identity that performed the action: a UPN or email address.

actor_id.label: Actor object id
actor_id.description: A stable, opaque id for the user, app or service principal that performed the action.

actor_ip.label: Actor IP address
actor_ip.description: The network address the request or sign-in came from.

app_id.label: Application id
app_id.description: The id of the client or service principal application involved in the record.

app_name.label: Application display name
app_name.description: The display name of the application involved in the record.

resource_id.label: Azure resource id
resource_id.description: The Azure Resource Manager path of the resource the record concerns, for example /subscriptions/.../providers/Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory.

resource_id_segment.label: Resource id segment
resource_id_segment.description: One named segment (subscription, resource group, provider or account) that the add-on extracts out of resourceId with its own EXTRACT.

event_time.label: Event time
event_time.description: When the action happened at the source, distinct from _time or TimeGenerated.

duration_ms.label: Duration (ms)
duration_ms.description: How long the operation or request took, in milliseconds.

outcome_result.label: Result
outcome_result.description: Whether the action succeeded, using the family's common result vocabulary.

result_reason.label: Result reason or description
result_reason.description: A human-readable explanation of the result: a failure reason, a display message or a detail string.

target_type.label: Target type
target_type.description: What kind of entity the record's target is.

target_id.label: Target id
target_id.description: The id of the entity the actor acted on. A record can carry more than one target.

target_name.label: Target display name
target_name.description: The display name of the entity the actor acted on.

risk_level.label: Risk level
risk_level.description: Microsoft Entra ID Protection's aggregated risk rating for the user or sign-in.

conditional_access_status.label: Conditional Access status
conditional_access_status.description: Whether a Conditional Access policy applied to the sign-in, and how. The cited schema page defines the related appliedConditionalAccessPolicies section but not this field by name, so the claim stays at what the sample showed.

geo_country.label: Sign-in country or region
geo_country.description: The country or region Microsoft Entra's geolocation maps the client address to.

geo_city.label: Sign-in city
geo_city.description: The city Microsoft Entra's geolocation maps the client address to.

device_id.label: Device id
device_id.description: The id of the device used for the sign-in, when the client reported one.

audit_event_id.label: Audit event id
audit_event_id.description: A unique id for one audit event.

actor_role_code.label: Actor type code
actor_role_code.description: A numeric code for what kind of actor performed the action (seen: 1, 3).

activity_type_code.label: Activity type or category code
activity_type_code.description: A numeric code the record carries for the activity's type or category (seen on ActivityType and Category).

change_type_cim.label: CIM change type
change_type_cim.description: The Splunk Common Information Model's own classification of the record, written by the add-on's EVAL, not by Azure.

object_category_cim.label: CIM object category
object_category_cim.description: The kind of object the add-on's Change/Audit CIM mapping says the record concerns.

service_name.label: Azure service or workload category
service_name.description: The Azure service or admin-center category a record came from, for example Core Directory, PIM or Azure Cosmos DB.

subscription_id.label: Subscription id
subscription_id.description: The Azure subscription a resource-log record belongs to.

azure_region.label: Azure region
azure_region.description: The Azure region the resource that emitted the record runs in.

client_user_agent.label: Client user agent
client_user_agent.description: The raw HTTP User-Agent string of the client that made the request.

cosmos_activity_id.label: Cosmos DB activity id
cosmos_activity_id.description: Azure Cosmos DB's own per-request id, distinct from the add-on's correlationId.

http_status_code.label: HTTP status code
http_status_code.description: The HTTP status code the Cosmos DB data-plane request returned.

request_charge_ru.label: Request charge (RU)
request_charge_ru.description: The number of Request Units the Cosmos DB operation consumed.

db_name.label: Database name
db_name.description: The Cosmos DB database the request targeted.

collection_name.label: Collection name
collection_name.description: The Cosmos DB container/collection the request targeted.

partition_id.label: Partition id
partition_id.description: The Cosmos DB physical partition that served the request.

vm_id.label: VM resource id (WADMetrics)
vm_id.description: The Azure Resource Manager id of the VM the metric row belongs to, colon-hex escaped in PartitionKey.

row_key.label: WADMetrics row key
row_key.description: Descending time tick and escaped counter path that uniquely identifies one metric row within its partition.

counter_name.label: Performance counter name
counter_name.description: The Windows or Linux performance counter path the row aggregates, matching the counterSpecifier in the diagnostics config.

metric_stat.label: Metric statistic
metric_stat.description: One statistic (maximum, minimum, total, count or average) of the counter over the aggregation period; which one is named on the binding.

metric_time.label: Metric row time
metric_time.description: The TIMESTAMP the add-on parses the aggregation period from. Not itself named on the cited vendor page; read from props.conf's TIME_PREFIX stanza for this sourcetype, not from data (the sourcetype carries no sample) or vendor prose.

azure:monitor:aad.description: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) sign-in, audit and risk records as the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services lands them from an Azure Event Hub diagnostic export: sign-ins (interactive, non-interactive, service principal, managed identity), directory AuditLogs, Microsoft Graph activity and Identity Protection risk events, all sharing one envelope.

azure:monitor:activity.description: Intune device-management audit events (Microsoft Graph's deviceManagement auditEvent resource, for example a device wipe or sync) as this Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services input lands them. Despite the sourcetype name this is not the general-purpose Azure Activity Log (Administrative, ServiceHealth and the other categories); that schema is carried by mscs:azure:audit in this environment.

mscs:azure:audit.description: Two different Azure audit shapes landing on one sourcetype: a Microsoft Entra directory-audit record wrapped in a body envelope, and a genuine Azure Activity Log Administrative-category record (authorization, claims, eventName, operationName, resourceProviderName) at the top level. Which shape a given event has depends on which fields are populated.

azure:monitor:resource.description: Azure resource (data-plane) diagnostic logs forwarded through an Event Hub, for example Azure Cosmos DB DataPlaneRequests: one record per data-plane operation, with the caller, the resource acted on, timing and (for Cosmos DB) request-unit cost.

mscs:vm:metrics.description: Azure Diagnostics (WAD) per-minute or per-hour VM performance-counter aggregates, read by the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services from the WADMetricsPT1M*/WADMetricsPT1H* Azure Table Storage tables: one row per counter per aggregation window, with its maximum, minimum, total, count and average.

time_basis.text: Several event-time fields (time, ActivityDate, activityDateTime, TIMESTAMP, eventTimestamp) can differ from _time; delivery to the workspace or storage lags the source event by minutes.

ip_shared.text: A NAT gateway, VPN exit or shared proxy can put many people behind one address; a match is a lead, not a link.

names_not_stable.text: A userPrincipalName, caller or display name survives an email change less often than an object id does; use the id to pivot.

guid_lookalikes.text: A record can carry several different GUIDs (tenant id, subscription id, app id, service principal id, correlation id, operation id) that are easy to swap by accident; check which one a query actually filters on.

numeric_code_undocumented.text: This numeric code is not defined on any Microsoft page found; the meaning given here is inferred from which values co-occur in the sample, not read from documentation.

multivalue_not_paired.text: Multivalue fields captured from a JSON array (the {} fields) are positional only if the source array was; a search-time operation on one {} field is not guaranteed to stay aligned with another.
